must_remember: Raman scattering is an instantaneous scattering process involving virtual energy states, unlike fluorescence which involves real absorption and re-emission.

Stokes lines have frequencies lower than the incident frequency ($
u_0 - 
u_m$), while anti-Stokes lines have higher frequencies ($
u_0 + 
u_m$).
The Raman shift ($\Delta \tilde{\nu}$) is entirely independent of the incident frequency $\nu_0$ and represents characteristic molecular vibrational or rotational frequencies.
At room temperature, the intensity of Stokes lines is greater than anti-Stokes lines because the ground state population exceeds the thermally excited state population.
Classically, Raman scattering arises from the modulation of molecular polarizability ($\alpha$) by molecular vibrations at frequency $\omega_m$.

glossary.meaning: Elastic scattering of light where the scattered photon has the same frequency $\nu_0$ as the incident photon.
Inelastic scattered spectral lines with lower frequency ($\nu_0 - \nu_m$) than the incident light.
Inelastic scattered spectral lines with higher frequency ($\nu_0 + \nu_m$) than the incident light, originating from thermally excited states.
The measure of ease with which an electron cloud of a molecule is distorted by an external electric field.
The difference between the wave number of the incident light and the scattered light, expressed in $\text{cm}^{-1}$.
